To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

democracies are more likely than non-democratic countries to support VNGOs, that the more democratic a country is the less likely it will support VNOs, that the more VNGO a country supports, the more likely that it will support other VNGOs, and that the more democratic the VNGO is the less likely that a country is to support it.
the more democratic the state, the less likely it is to support VNGOs that fight other states in general, and the more so if the VNGOs fight democracies in particular

democracies are significantly less warlike by means of supporting VNGOs warring against other states than non-democratic regimes, and the more the democratic character of the regime, the lower the probability of its supporting VNGOs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether democracies are less likely to support VNGOs than non-democracies.
the relationship between regime type, support to violent non-state actors, and the nature of the target.
the question whether democracies are warlike by proxy, and if so, to what extent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
democracies do support VNGOs less than autocracies do.
democracies are less likely to support VNGOs that wage war against other states than autocracies.
democracies do support VNGOs less than non-democracies, but that this support is more likely to occur when the VNGOs wage war against non-democracies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
democracies are more likely to support VNGOs than non-democratic regimes, but they do so less than non-democracies.
the more democratic the state is, the more peaceful it is in its relations with other states and with VNGOs.
democracies do not fight indirectly through material VNGOs support, while non-democracies do.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the democratic peace is not only an interstate phenomenon but it is also an intrastate one.
the more democratic a regime is the less likely it is to support violent non-governmental organisations waging war against another state.
democracies do not support VNGOs in intrastate conflicts.
